item.title: Mapping 20-years winter wheat dynamics in global primary planting areas using Gaussian mixture models with adaptive thresholds
item.description:
Mapping 20-years winter wheat dynamics in global primary planting areas using Gaussian mixture models with adaptive thresholds
Yanan Wen, Tuo Chen, Xuecao Li, Tiecheng Bai, Ke Yao, Liheng Zhong, Han Chen, Meiling Liu, Xieqin Huang, Shunlin Liang, Shuangxi Miao, and Jianxi Huang
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 8311–8328, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-8311-2026, 2026
We developed a new method to track winter wheat growth across the world from 2001 to 2020. Using satellite data, we produced high-resolution maps (1 km) that show exactly where and how much winter wheat was planted over the last two decades. The results proved to be highly accurate when compared against international agricultural records. As the first long-term, global view of its kind, this map series is a vital tool for scientists and policymakers working to eliminate hunger.

item.title: PhaFoS: a global database of Phanerozoic foraminiferal size
item.description:
PhaFoS: a global database of Phanerozoic foraminiferal size
Yan Feng, Jiankang Lai, Daoliang Chu, Xiaokang Liu, Xiang Shu, Lee Hsiang Liow, Yuyang Wu, Yunfei Huang, and Haijun Song
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 8329–8344, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-8329-2026, 2026
How has the size of tiny marine organisms changed throughout Earth's history? We have created a global database of body sizes covering 118 885 specimens of foraminifera – single-celled organisms with a rich fossil record. By linking test size to the time and location at which these organisms lived, the database enables researchers to track long-term size changes across ancient oceans and investigate their relationship with environmental change.

item.title: A global 0.05° dataset of daily latent heat flux and resistances (2001–2020) derived via the Energy-Resistance-Coupling framework
item.description:
A global 0.05° dataset of daily latent heat flux and resistances (2001–2020) derived via the Energy-Resistance-Coupling framework
Lingfei Zhang, Xiaowei Wang, Yazhen Jiang, Shuqing Wang, Menglin Si, and Cheng Huang
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-678,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
We developed a daily global dataset describing latent heat flux and the resistances that regulate land–atmosphere water and energy exchange from 2001 to 2020 at 0.05° resolution. The product was evaluated against 244 flux-tower sites and performs robustly across climates and ecosystems. It provides new information for studying drought, ecosystem water stress, land–atmosphere coupling, and Earth system models.

item.title: ChinaMet: A multisource integrated high-resolution multi-variable meteorological dataset for China
item.description:
ChinaMet: A multisource integrated high-resolution multi-variable meteorological dataset for China
Yingyi Hu, Ling Zhang, Yanbo Zhao, and Tao Che
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-704,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
ChinaMet is a high-resolution meteorological dataset for China covering 1980–2024. It integrates over 2,300 station observations with satellite, reanalysis, and auxiliary data through a merging–downscaling framework, providing eight variables at 0.01° resolution. ChinaMet offers continuous and spatially detailed meteorological forcing for hydrological, ecological, agricultural, and climate applications.
